node.title: Re: i2c bus contention
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I considered having a lock file that each script accesses, to control access to the i2c bus, but that seems like a lot of overhead, probably worse that my time slot solution.

Taking a brief look at [https://metacpan.org/source/MDOOTSON/HiPi-0.80/I2C.xs#L235|the code], it appears that what [mod://HiPi::Device::I2C] is doing is an [doc://ioctl] on the /dev/i2c* device file, and my guess would be that the Linux kernel doesn't guarantee those to be atomic when there are multiple writers. But I also don't see your issue with a lock file, since I2C writes should be pretty quick - why not just [doc://flock] the object's filehandle? I don't have an RPi with an I2C device handy to test, but I'd suggest just trying something like this:

use Fcntl qw/:flock/; ... my $i2c = HiPi::Device::I2C->new(...); ... flock($i2c->fh, LOCK_EX) or die "flock: $!"; $i2c->bus_write(...); flock($i2c->fh, LOCK_UN) or die "flock: $!";
